```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 9,
                     fig.height = 6, warning = TRUE)
```

The two plotting functions read **already saved** evaluation curves. Neither
function fits a model, recalibrates predictions, searches for a useful cutoff,
or calculates a missing curve. All data and thresholds below are synthetic
demonstrations, not clinical evidence or recommended treatment thresholds.

```{r load}
library(stormbreaker)
predictors <- c("gene_a", "gene_b")
thresholds <- c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7)
```

Plotting requires the optional `ggplot2` package. If unavailable, install it
with `install.packages("ggplot2")`; core fitting and tables do not require it.

## Binary development results

Declare the DCA thresholds in the development task, before fitting or inspecting
external outcomes. An outcome-blind final prediction carries this declaration
forward to external evaluation.

```{r binary-cv}
binary_data <- bi_example(120, seed = 1)
binary_task <- bi_task(
  binary_data, "patient_id", "outcome", predictors,
  decision_thresholds = thresholds
)
binary_pipeline <- sb_pipeline(learner = "logistic")
binary_cv <- run_cv(binary_task, binary_pipeline, folds = 3, seed = 1)
```

```{r binary-calibration}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(plot_calib(binary_cv))
}
```

Binary calibration compares predicted class-1 probability with the **saved
smoothed descriptive estimate** of observed probability. The dashed diagonal
is ideal calibration, not a fitted model. The curve is not applied to future
predictions, and no uncertainty band is inferred by the plotting function.

```{r binary-dca}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(plot_dca(binary_cv))
}
```

DCA shows net benefit for the model, treating all, and treating none at each
saved threshold. Negative net benefit remains visible. Points mark the actual
thresholds; lines only connect them. A higher line in this demonstration is
not evidence that a treatment or threshold should be selected clinically.

## Binary external evaluation

Fit the predeclared model on development data. Predict the external feature
table without its outcome, then separately match and evaluate the saved
predictions using external outcomes.

```{r binary-external}
binary_fit <- fit_final(binary_task, binary_pipeline)
binary_external <- bi_example(100, seed = 2)
binary_external$patient_id <- paste0("EXT_", binary_external$patient_id)
binary_prediction <- predict_final(
  binary_fit, binary_external[c("patient_id", predictors)],
  id_col = "patient_id"
)
binary_endpoint <- bi_endpoint(binary_external, "patient_id", "outcome")
binary_evaluation <- eval_external(binary_prediction, binary_endpoint)
```

```{r binary-external-calibration}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(plot_calib(binary_evaluation, cohort_label = "Synthetic holdout"))
}
```

```{r binary-external-dca}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(plot_dca(binary_evaluation, cohort_label = "Synthetic holdout"))
}
```

The label helps identify the data, but cannot prove external validity or
independence. Both the source evaluation boundary and the label remain visible.
Do not choose the final model or its thresholds using these external results.

## Survival development and external results

The task explicitly specifies the prediction horizon and time unit. Survival
calibration is displayed on the **event-probability** scale at that horizon,
using columns already present in the saved curve; it is not an S(t) curve.
Survival DCA likewise uses event probability by the horizon and preserves the
existing censoring-aware estimator.

```{r survival-cv}
survival_data <- surv_example(120, seed = 1)
survival_task <- surv_task(
  survival_data, "patient_id", "time", "event", predictors, "month",
  prediction_horizon = 6, decision_thresholds = thresholds
)
survival_pipeline <- sb_pipeline()
survival_cv <- run_cv(survival_task, survival_pipeline, folds = 3, seed = 1)
```

```{r survival-calibration}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(plot_calib(survival_cv))
}
```

```{r survival-dca}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(plot_dca(survival_cv))
}
```

```{r survival-external}
survival_fit <- fit_final(survival_task, survival_pipeline)
survival_external <- surv_example(100, seed = 2)
survival_external$patient_id <- paste0("EXT_", survival_external$patient_id)
survival_prediction <- predict_final(
  survival_fit, survival_external[c("patient_id", predictors)],
  id_col = "patient_id"
)
survival_endpoint <- surv_endpoint(
  survival_external, "patient_id", "time", "event", "month",
  prediction_horizon = 6
)
survival_evaluation <- eval_external(survival_prediction, survival_endpoint)
```

```{r survival-external-calibration}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(plot_calib(survival_evaluation, cohort_label = "Synthetic holdout"))
}
```

```{r survival-external-dca}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(plot_dca(survival_evaluation, cohort_label = "Synthetic holdout"))
}
```

For methods and assumptions inspect the original
`survival_evaluation$metrics$calibration` and
`survival_evaluation$metrics$decision_curve` objects. Plotting does not change
their statistical definitions or censoring assumptions.

## Comparisons remain one panel per model

Single shared-fold comparisons and single-cohort external comparisons are also
accepted. They retain the supplied pipeline order. Each DCA panel uses that
pipeline's own saved reference strategies; no cross-cohort mixing is performed.

```{r comparison, fig.height=9}
compared <- compare_cv(
  binary_task,
  list(binary_pipeline, sb_pipeline(learner = "gaussian_naive_bayes")),
  folds = 3, seed = 1
)
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(plot_dca(compared))
}
```

## Missing requests and failures are not silent

A task that did not declare DCA thresholds cannot acquire a DCA result merely
by plotting. Default plots omit unusable methods and their empty panels;
if none are usable, an explicit no-results message is displayed. Set
`show_unavailable = TRUE` to retain diagnostic panels. No curve is invented.
Survival calibration likewise needs a previously declared horizon.

```{r not-requested}
plain_task <- bi_task(binary_data, "patient_id", "outcome", predictors)
plain_cv <- run_cv(plain_task, binary_pipeline, folds = 3, seed = 1)
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  p <- plot_dca(plain_cv)
  print(p)
  attr(p, "stormbreaker_curve_status")
}
```

`metric_status` and `run_status` are separate. If the whole run failed at
another output, this initial plotting interface still withholds the curve;
the saved coordinates remain in `attr(plot, "stormbreaker_curve_data")` and
the original result. Default `plot$data` contains displayed pipelines only. No
failure is relabeled as success. Missing information following a failure is
distinguished from an unrequested analysis.

Only finite, usable coordinates of successful curves and runs are drawn.
Missing rows break line segments; they are not filled or bridged. Per-pipeline
diagnostics are available with `attr(plot, "stormbreaker_curve_status")`, while
the source retains the complete fitted state and statistical assumptions.
Use `sb_failure_table(plain_cv)` or `sb_export_failures(plain_cv,
"new-failures.csv")` for separate saved issue records. Unrequested curves are
not counted as failures. Review saved error text before sharing the CSV.

These functions do not yet accept repeated CV, stacking or multi-cohort
collections, and do not implement time-dependent ROC, KM, nomograms, competing
risks or bootstrap confidence ribbons. Neither function writes files; customize
and save the returned ggplot explicitly when needed.
